Hi Samir —

Great to meet earlier today. Quick recap from our discovery and a few items we need to lock down so we can put together concrete pricing and an SOW draft: 

1) Expected monthly token volume (please confirm an expected range and any seasonality).
2) Peak TPS / concurrency profile (sustained vs short bursts, and typical burst duration).
3) Target $/1M tokens or budget range you’re aiming for (helps us propose committed vs pay-as-you-go options).
4) Any hard constraints on latency/SLA or data residency.

Notes from the call: OptiHealth is primarily inference-heavy on short classification calls (prompt+completion ~120 tokens average) but also has periodic long-report generation flows (~1.2k tokens) for diagnostics. You mentioned a month 1 pilot to validate volume shape.

Attached I’m including a small pricing scenario workbook (redwood_pricing_examples.xlsx) and a very initial SOW template (SOW-OptiHealth-draft.pdf) — both are placeholders while we confirm volumes.

Ask: can you confirm the monthly range and the expected peak TPS window (e.g., 5–10 minute bursts vs sustained minutes)? If you can reply here today/early tomorrow we’ll run the cost models and send a short comparison of two options (committed discount vs on-demand).

Proposed next step: 30-minute alignment call Wednesday 9/3 to walk numbers and finalize pilot commit. I’ll send a calendar invite once we have a time that works.

Thanks,
Soojin

Thanks, Soojin — appreciate the summary. A few quick answers from our side: 

- Monthly token estimate: 30M–50M tokens/month for the first 6 months (pilot -> ramp), with steady-state expectation around 80M within 12 months if the pilot succeeds.
- Peak TPS: we see short bursts up to ~120 TPS (burst windows ~3–7 minutes) for live inference during high-traffic windows, plus an intermittent background batch process that can spike to ~60 TPS for ~30 minutes. Sustained baseline is ~15–25 TPS.
- Budget target: we’re looking to stay in the $12–$18 / 1M tokens band for committed pricing; for POC we could accept slightly higher on-demand pricing.
- SLA/data residency: US only; standard enterprise SLAs preferred but we can accept a pilot-level SLA for the first 30 days.

Procurement asked for an example invoice and simple cost scenarios (committed vs on-demand) — can you include a 3-line example calculation showing monthly spend at 30M and 50M tokens? Also curious how peak TPS is handled (burst capacity vs autoscaling) and any overage pricing.

Samir

Hi Samir —

Thanks for the quick details — useful ranges. A few pricing/operational notes to help procurement: 

1) Mapping TPS to pricing: peak TPS affects capacity planning but does not directly change the $/1M token rate unless you need guaranteed dedicated capacity. For most hosted customers, we offer committed token discounts (monthly commits) and autoscaling that covers short bursts.

2) Example scenarios (ballpark):
  - Option A (Committed): 40M tokens/month commit -> $12 / 1M tokens -> ~$480 / month for the first line-item (note: this is illustrative). Peak bursting is supported up to 150 TPS across the shared pool for short windows; sustained high TPS may require a Dedicated pool add-on.
  - Option B (On-demand): no commit -> $18 / 1M tokens -> ~$720 / month at 40M tokens; simpler to start a POC.

3) Overage and burst: bursts that exceed autoscaling thresholds are billed as normal tokens but very short bursts (<5m) are usually absorbed by transient capacity. If you need guaranteed concurrency (no throttling), we can propose a burst reserve or Dedicated overlay — we’d price that separately.

4) Cost examples (as Samir requested):
  - 30M tokens/month at $12/1M = $360/month
  - 50M tokens/month at $12/1M = $600/month
  - 30M tokens/month at $18/1M = $540/month
  - 50M tokens/month at $18/1M = $900/month

I’ll drop a short spreadsheet into the deal record with a couple more permutations (I referenced the same redwood_pricing_examples.xlsx Soojin shared). Also linking an internal doc that describes autoscaling/burst handling: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/OPTI-2026-0043 (internal link).

If these ranges look OK, we can draft a 3-month pilot SOW (40M commit at pilot-rate, with a 30-day exit) and include a burst-reserve appendix.

Best,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
